messages.subject: Infinite rollback
parts:
Hi there, 

I try to rollback arrivals based on some conditions. I only want to let the arrival through that has an attribute (id) that is equal to the 'optimal' id (optIdRegion1). This optIdRegion1 is update globally using find_opt_id() once an arrival is released by a resource (pickOperatorRegion1). Then, once new arrivals arrive, I only want that the arrival with attribute 'id' equal to optIdRegion1 goes through the rollback and all other arrivals should rollback. 

So basically, I want to select which arrival may seize the resource. For the other arrivals, I want them to wait upon pickOperatorRegion1 is released, and then I want to re-evaluate which one to have the resource seized.

Currently I used a rollback function (see below) but the problem is that arrivals are infinitely looping when timeout is 0 (i.e., no event occurs). It works when I set timeout to 0.1 let's say but the problem is that this 1) undesirable in terms of activity time and 2) in terms of computation time as all arrivals keep on looping.

So probably the use of a rollback is not the way to go for this particular problem. What would be the right way to model this situation where no FCFS principle is used?


env <- simmer("Environment")
env

pickingRegion1Trajectory <- trajectory("Picking Process") %>%
  seize("pickOperatorRegion1") %>%
  log_(function() paste("Capacity set to", get_capacity(env, "pickRegion1"))) %>%
  timeout_from_attribute("historicalPickingTime") %>% 
  release("pickOperatorRegion1") %>%
  release("pickRegion1") %>%
  timeout(function() find_opt_id()) %>%
  set_capacity("pickRegion1", 1) %>%
  log_(function() paste("Capacity set to", get_capacity(env, "pickRegion1")))


region1QueueTraject <- trajectory("Arrivals looping in queue unless the arrival is the optimal arrival") %>%
  log_(function() paste("My id is", get_attribute(env, "id"), "and I am in region 1")) %>%
  timeout(0) %>%
  rollback(2, check= function() get_attribute(env, "id") != optIdRegion1) %>%
  
  seize("pickRegion1") %>%
  set_capacity("pickRegion1", 0) %>%
  timeout(function() remove_opt_from_regionqueu1()) %>%
  join(pickingRegion1Trajectory)


env %>% 
  add_dataframe("job", queueVoedTrajectory, mockJobData, mon = 2, batch =50,
              col_time = "time", time = "absolute",
              col_attributes = c("arrivalMoment", "size", "cutOff", "historicalPickingTime", "historicalPackingTime", "transportationTime", "outboundLine"))
env %>% 
add_resource("pickOperatorRegion1", nPickersRegion1, 0) %>%

add_resource("pickRegion1", 1)

env %>% run(50) %>%
  now()  

env %>% get_mon_arrivals()
env %>% get_mon_resources()

Kind regards

If I understood correctly, you are using rollback() as a kind of wait
mechanism until some condition is met, right? That's not the purpose
of a rollback. Instead, use proper signalling using trap(), wait(),
send().

>
>
> env <- simmer("Environment")
> env
>
> pickingRegion1Trajectory <- trajectory("Picking Process") %>%
> seize("pickOperatorRegion1") %>%
> log_(function() paste("Capacity set to", get_capacity(env, "pickRegion1"))) %>%
> timeout_from_attribute("historicalPickingTime") %>%
> release("pickOperatorRegion1") %>%
> release("pickRegion1") %>%
> timeout(function() find_opt_id()) %>%
> set_capacity("pickRegion1", 1) %>%
> log_(function() paste("Capacity set to", get_capacity(env, "pickRegion1")))
>
>
> region1QueueTraject <- trajectory("Arrivals looping in queue unless the arrival is the optimal arrival") %>%
> log_(function() paste("My id is", get_attribute(env, "id"), "and I am in region 1")) %>%
> timeout(0) %>%
> rollback(2, check= function() get_attribute(env, "id") != optIdRegion1) %>%
>
> seize("pickRegion1") %>%
> set_capacity("pickRegion1", 0) %>%
> timeout(function() remove_opt_from_regionqueu1()) %>%
> join(pickingRegion1Trajectory)
>
>
> env %>%
> add_dataframe("job", queueVoedTrajectory, mockJobData, mon = 2, batch =50,
> col_time = "time", time = "absolute",
> col_attributes = c("arrivalMoment", "size", "cutOff", "historicalPickingTime", "historicalPackingTime", "transportationTime", "outboundLine"))

> add_resource("pickOperatorRegion1", nPickersRegion1, 0) %>%
>
> add_resource("pickRegion1", 1)
>
> env %>% run(50) %>%
> now()
>
> env %>% get_mon_arrivals()
> env %>% get_mon_resources()
>
> Kind regards

parts:
Thanks for the response!

Currtently I have two resources in series: 1) pickRegion1 with inf queue that is supposed to have the arrivals 'wait' and 2) pickOperatorRegion1 with queue zero that will actually process the arrival. Based on your response I suppose I could get rid of the first resource and use wait() instead. However, upon releasing pickOperatorRegion1 I want the signal to be sent to only one specific arrival (the one with it's attribute 'id' equal to optIdRegion1). Then, I need to access the attributes of the arrivals 'in' wait(). Can this be done? If yes, how could such a condition be set-up?

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Infinite rollback

On Tue, 7 Apr 2020 at 08:58, Eras <j.e...@student.tue.nl> wrote:
>
> Thanks for the response!
>
> Currtently I have two resources in series: 1) pickRegion1 with inf queue that is supposed to have the arrivals 'wait' and 2) pickOperatorRegion1 with queue zero that will actually process the arrival. Based on your response I suppose I could get rid of the first resource and use wait() instead.

> However, upon releasing pickOperatorRegion1 I want the signal to be sent to only one specific arrival (the one with it's attribute 'id' equal to optIdRegion1). Then, I need to access the attributes of the arrivals 'in' wait(). Can this be done? If yes, how could such a condition be set-up?

Forget about the arrivals' attribute. Arrivals need to trap() a signal
with a unique identifier, i.e., their id, and wait(). Then, the
released arrival must calculate the next optimal id and send() that
specific signal, so that only that arrival continues.


--
Iñaki Úcar
